title: Felix and the Orchard
premise: Xanthe Dunmore inherited her family's failing vineyard along with crushing debts, and she has sworn off love since a betrayal she blames herself for. When the local harvest festival's anonymous pen-pal program pairs her with 'Felix' — who turns out to be Elias Vane, the bank's foreclosure officer and her oldest rival — their letters become the one place they can be honest while their waking war escalates over the orchard adjoining her vines, which he is ordered to seize. As Xanthe uncovers proof that Elias's superiors forged documents to steal the orchard from its rightful heirs, she must choose between saving her vineyard through a ruthless deal or exposing the fraud at the cost of everything she has left. In the end, she forgives herself for the past, testifies beside Elias against his own employer, and the two of them replant the orchard together — love no longer in the past tense.
about_author: Xanthe Oyelaran spent six years managing a smallholding orchard in the English countryside before turning to fiction full-time. Her novels explore how inheritance — of land, debt, and guilt — shapes the heart's capacity to begin again.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Opening with a failed harvest audit, Xanthe confronts the vineyard's ledgers and the memory of the fiancé who left when the debts surfaced. She signs up for the town's anonymous pen-pal festival on a dare from her foreman, telling herself it's harmless. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Letter That Shouldn't Fit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Her first anonymous letter arrives — witty, wounded, unexpectedly kind — and she answers too honestly before she can stop herself. Meanwhile Elias Vane appears at her gate with foreclosure papers for the neighboring orchard. Emotional beat: a crack of warmth in an armored day.

chapters.title: Enemy at the Gate
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias recognizes Xanthe's handwriting immediately; he wrote to her deliberately, hoping to soften her before the seizure. But her reply unsettles him more than any argument. He pushes the foreclosure timeline anyway. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Walking the disputed orchard, Xanthe finds an old deed fragment suggesting the land was taken unjustly decades ago — and that her own father may have witnessed it. She begins investigating while her letters with 'Felix' deepen. Emotional beat: curiosity rekindling purpose.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the midsummer fair, letters are meant to be revealed; instead, Xanthe glimpses Elias posting hers and realizes Felix is her enemy. She says nothing, testing him through the letters while waging open war by day. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Forged Seal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the deed trail, Xanthe discovers the bank's regional director fabricated transfer documents generations ago — and Elias's current order rests on that rot. She confronts Elias privately; he claims ignorance but cannot deny the seal. Emotional beat: fury colliding with reluctant belief.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The director offers Elias a promotion if he closes the seizure quietly and buries the old records. Torn, Elias nearly accepts — until he rereads every letter Felix received and understands he has been falling for Xanthe all along. Emotional beat: the cost of complicity made personal.

chapters.title: Ash Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A suspicious fire damages the orchard's record barn, destroying half the evidence; the director frames Xanthe for arson, and her vineyard's license is suspended. Standing in the smoke, she almost gives up — then chooses to fight outside the law's broken channels. Emotional beat: despair transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Letters
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the public harvest hearing, Xanthe reveals Felix's identity and reads their letters aloud as testimony, while Elias produces the surviving deed copy he secretly preserved, turning witness against his employer. The director's fraud unravels publicly. Emotional beat: climax — truth spoken where it hurts most.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, the orchard is returned to its rightful heirs, Xanthe's name cleared, her debts restructured into a cooperative with the restored families. On the first day of planting season, she and Elias write each other one final signed letter — then read them side by side under the new trees. Emotional beat: forgiveness, of self and other, taking root.
